---
title: "Episodic Structure in Psychotic Discourse: A Reproducible Workflow for Modeling Meta-Communication and Delusional Ontology in Schreber's Memoirs"
date: last-modified
lang: en

abstract: |
  This study presents a reproducible computational workflow for analysing psychotic discourse through the interaction between meta-communication and delusional ontology. Building on pragmatic communication theory, these dimensions are operationalized as paragraph-level textual features and combined into a coupling index, enabling the examination of temporal organization in extended narrative material. Applied to Schreber's *Memoirs of My Nervous Illness*, the analysis tests competing models of psychotic discourse, including cumulative escalation, temporal clustering, and reactive coupling. The results do not support a global escalation account. Instead, they reveal a non-uniform and temporally heterogeneous structure characterised by weak global association, limited serial persistence, and a small number of localized high-coupling segments. These peaks correspond to episodic configurations in which meta-communicative framing and delusional ontology become selectively aligned. The findings suggest that psychotic discourse is better understood as a sequence of transient discursive regimes rather than as a continuously intensifying system. Methodologically, the workflow provides a transparent and extensible framework for integrating qualitative theory with quantitative text analysis. Theoretically, it offers a preliminary formal framework for testing selected discourse-level implications of phenomenological models, particularly Sass's concept of hyperreflexivity, in an empirically tractable form.
